protein stability toward organic solvent/waters emulsification is a critical issue that needs to be taken into account for protein microencapsulated into microspheres by the W/O/W emulsion technique.
the organic solvent/wate interface can be an environment that is not conducive to protein integrity and the extent of damage depends on the nature of the protein and the solvent used.
the organic solvent/wate rinterface was detrimental to protein stability, and that the emulsification step was a major contributor to protein denaturing effects during the microencapsulation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of proteins in an organic solvent/wate interface and the implications for protein microcapsules.
the development of a microencapsulation method that is capable of preserving protein integrity.
the stability and integrity of proteins at the organic solvent/wate interface and the implications for protein microcapsulation into microspheres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emulsification process should be optimized to reduce protein denaturation and the formation of covalently bound water-insoluble aggregates.
protein microencapsulation in organic solvent/water microspheres should be performed at the lowest temperature possible and in the presence of a protein stabilizer.
the organic solvent/wate interface is a harsh environment for protein molecules and the extent of damage is protein dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organic solvent should be carefully selected for the purpose of microencapsulation.
a protein with a higher propensity for aggregation is more likely to undergo emulsification-induced aggregation.
the protein microencapsulation process should be designed in such a way to minimize the exposure of proteins to organic solvents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of organic solvent is crucial in the microencapsulation of proteins.
the choice of organic solvent should be based on the protein type to be encapsulated.
the use of organic solvents in protein microencapsulation should be avoided, or at least used cautiously.
